segments.note: Title retains the universal coverage requirement; given/then retain the exact frontend scope and binding requirement.
Summary is consolidated into the title without losing the coverage requirement; exact scope remains in given/then.

activation.note: Activation preserves exposed entrypoints with frontend or undeclared surfaces, internal/backend exclusions, excluded scan trees, and qualifying bindings and URNs. Path matching identifies candidates rather than establishing coverage; the full browser-spec definition remains in verifier_detail. Semantic parsing and cross-reference findings are explicitly marked needs_new_observer, rather than claimed observable from paths alone.

audit.summary: All 21 segments survive at their claimed destinations, with only duplicate title/summary wording compressed. The rewrite retains one coverage obligation, the original exceptions, and the browser-spec recognition rules without introducing waivers or application-specific requirements.

segmentChecks.note: The title compresses the name, while given/then restore the exact exposed-entrypoint, frontend-or-undeclared-surfaces scope and the E2E/SMOKE requirement.
The summary duplicates the name; its universal coverage obligation remains in the title and normative then clause without loss.
Given, then, activation, and verifier_detail jointly retain both surface cases, exposed entrypoints, the // Journey binding, and the qualifying URN kinds.
Verifier_detail[0] preserves the Playwright/*.e2e.ts alternative, all four header-marker forms, and treatment of misnamed test files; activation also identifies the needed parser.
Verifier_detail[1], avoid[0], and activation explicitly state that a string-only journey URN mention in a unit test neither counts as a browser spec nor suppresses a finding.
Why and avoid[1] retain the distinction between route-level decision tests and browser end-to-end journey coverage.
Unless[1], verifier_detail[4], and activation preserve all four excluded trees and clarify that candidates there cannot provide coverage.
Unless[0], doesNotFire, and verifier_detail[2] retain both internal journeys and exposed journeys whose surfaces exclude frontend, including the backend example.

risks: The coder-facing fields do not give the exact E2E/SMOKE test-URN syntax or explicitly require Playwright execution for a conventionally named *.e2e.ts file; a coder implementing recognition rather than following the preferred fix could accept a nonqualifying file unless it consults verifier_detail.

The coder-facing fields mention journey-marker headers generally but list only // Journey: explicitly; the alternative // Train: and // URN: marker forms are available only in verifier_detail and activation.

unobservable: Journey definitions, entrypoint exposure, and declared surfaces require a journey-definition observer.
Header-comment journey markers and // Journey: bindings require source/header parsing rather than path facts.
Whether a test URN is E2E or SMOKE and the resulting per-journey coverage finding require semantic cross-referencing.
Whether a *.e2e.ts file is actually run by Playwright is not established by path_glob alone.

review.summary: All sampled knowledge survives at its destinations, including the two justified title/summary compressions, and the rewrite preserves the original scope and exclusions without waiver creep. Activation is deterministic once its explicitly declared semantic observers exist; the only residual usability risk is that some detailed browser-spec recognition syntax sits outside the coder-facing fields.
